card.occupation: Part-time replenishment assistant (shelf stacker) on early-morning shifts at a large supermarket, about 24 hours a week over four mornings
card.education_detail: Left a local secondary school at 16 with a handful of GCSEs (passed English, scraped maths at the second go). Started a hairdressing course at college and dropped out after the first year. Has done the supermarket's in-house food safety and manual handling training, and nothing formal since.
card.household: Rents a two-bed ex-council terraced house with her partner Dean, 52, a self-employed scaffolder. They've been together 21 years and never got round to marrying, which neither of them sees much point in. Their son Kieran, 23, moved out last year to share a flat in Maidstone with his girlfriend. There's an elderly Staffordshire bull terrier called Roxy.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in north Kent. Her dad worked at the paper mill and her mum did school dinners. Christened Church of England. She calls herself Christian and means it in a background sort of way: she'd say she believes in God, but she only goes to church for weddings, funerals and sometimes the Christmas Eve carol service if her mum asks. She's lived within ten miles of where she grew up her whole life.
card.professional_persona: Gets the job done fast but not tidily, and sees the job as a means to an end. Her shift starts at 5am and she's late more often than her manager would like, but she shifts stock quicker than most. She doesn't do workplace politics or pretend to like people she doesn't. She has had a couple of 'informal chats' about her attitude with a team leader she thinks is useless. She likes finishing at 11 and having the rest of the day.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks Roxy round the rec most days, and there's enough lifting at work that she doesn't see the need for a gym. She'll watch the football with Dean if Gillingham are doing anything, mostly for the pub atmosphere. She did netball at school and was 'too gobby for it' according to the PE teacher.
card.arts_persona: Watches a lot of telly: true crime documentaries, Gogglebox, anything with people arguing on it. Listens to Heart or Kiss in the car and still likes the 90s dance music she went out to as a teenager. Reads the odd crime paperback on holiday and never finishes it. She isn't interested in galleries or theatre, though she has been to a couple of panto nights with her sister's kids.
card.travel_persona: One week abroad a year if money allows, usually somewhere all-inclusive in Spain or Turkey booked last-minute, often after a row about who was supposed to sort it. She's been to Tenerife four times. Weekends in a caravan at Camber or Leysdown. She doesn't have a valid passport half the time because she forgets to renew it.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks quick, unfussy dinners: spag bol, chicken in a jar sauce, oven chips and something, or a roast on Sundays if Kieran's coming. Friday is a takeaway, usually Chinese. She's not bothered about food trends and thinks air fryers are the best thing that's happened in years. She drinks tea strong with one sugar and likes a rosé at the weekend.
hobbies_and_interests: Walking the dog round the rec and along the creek
Scratchcards and the odd bingo night with her sister
Car boot sales on a Sunday when she can be bothered to get up
Facebook local community groups, mainly for the arguments
skills: Fast, physically strong worker on a stockroom floor
Can drive and reverse a van, as she sometimes helps Dean out
Basic hairdressing: cuts Dean's and her nephews' hair
Good at haggling at boot sales
Unflappable in a crisis, as nothing much rattles her
Pretty handy with the supermarket handheld scanners and stock systems
card.career_goals: Hasn't got any to speak of. She'd like more money for the same hours, and might go for a team leader role if it came up, mostly for the pay. Sometimes says she'd like to do mobile hairdressing on her own terms but hasn't done anything about it. She's mainly aiming to keep her mornings-only shifts and not have to work weekends.
card.voice: Plain, direct, fairly quick, with a north Kent/Estuary accent: dropped t's, 'yeah' a lot. Uses 'erm' when she's thinking but doesn't dwell. Uses 'sort of' as a hedge, and 'to be honest' before saying something blunt. Ends some sentences with 'you know' or 'know what I mean'. She'll say 'you was' occasionally without noticing, says 'dinner' for the evening meal, and calls herself 'knackered' after a shift. Gives short answers to questions she thinks are pointless and longer ones if something annoys her. She doesn't fill silences; she'll just wait, or say 'that's it really' and stop.
card.typing: All lowercase, minimal punctuation and no full stops at the end. Often drops apostrophes: dont, cant, im. Short answers, sometimes just 'yeah' or 'not really'. Uses 'tbh' and 'idk' now and then. The odd typo she doesn't correct. Will put 'n/a' if she can't be bothered with a question.
card.with_strangers: Comes across as a bit guarded and no-nonsense at first, not unfriendly but not trying to impress anyone. She'll be polite enough but won't laugh at jokes she doesn't find funny, and she'll say so if a question seems daft. Warms up if the other person is straightforward with her. She's not easily embarrassed and isn't nervous about being on a call.
small_things: Getting up at 4:15 for her shift and being in bed by half nine
Roxy's dodgy hips and the vet bills
The state of the roads round Sittingbourne and the roadworks on the A2
Something she saw in a local Facebook group
Her sister's kids and what they've been up to
deeper_things: Her mum's getting forgetful and Tracey's the one who ends up taking her to appointments, even though she and her sister don't really get on about it
She misses having Kieran at home more than she lets on, though she'd never say it to him
Money's tighter than it looks: they've had letters about missed council tax payments because she forgot to set up the direct debit
She sometimes wonders if she should have finished the hairdressing course
She and Dean have talked about whether they'll ever buy a house, and both know it probably won't happen
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a kitchen table, angled slightly upward so the ceiling light is visible at the top edge. Flat, overhead artificial light plus some grey daylight from a window to the left. Woman in her late forties with a fair, slightly weathered complexion, light freckles, faint lines around the eyes and mouth. Expression neutral, mouth closed, one eyebrow slightly raised as if waiting. Shoulder-length hair, dyed dark blonde with about an inch of brown roots, scraped back loosely in a claw clip with strands falling at the sides. No glasses. Small gold hoop earrings. Wearing a navy zip-up fleece over a grey T-shirt. Behind her: a white kitchen wall with a calendar from a local Chinese takeaway pinned up, a wall clock, part of a fridge-freezer covered in magnets and a dentist's appointment card, and a worktop with a kettle, an air fryer and a stack of unopened post. A dog's lead hangs on a hook by the back door, which is partly visible on the right.
